question: Can a lightly gated recurrent arithmetic checkpoint adapt to closed thinking turns on ordinary GSM8K questions while retaining language quality?
training: Take the first 128 previously reserved train rows whose complete zero-demo thinking prompt and publisher natural-language rationale fit 224 positions. Remove duplicate calculator markup. Supervise rationale, close-think, numeric final and chat end. Restore Phase 4 parent weights, fresh AdamW on its gate and shared middle LoRA, K2, activation checkpointing. No new base weights.
evaluation: Reuse 32 previously scored, training-disjoint GSM8K development questions. Same zero-demo thinking chat for both arms, unrestricted greedy decoding up to 256 tokens, stop at first EOS or official chat end. Require one closed thinking span, completed first turn and unambiguous numeric answer. Score all items in frozen order. Compare the deployment to unchanged Base K1. The pre-existing Phase 4 matched dense control is preserved; no attribution to recurrence.
gate: Require candidate >=8/32 correct, positive net wins on both prespecified halves, >=4 net wins overall, elapsed generation time <=1.25 times Base, and token-weighted V3 prose NLL <= Base + 0.03. Report each domain. All conditions required for a fresh held-out replication. A memory, iteration or time limit interrupts work and closes dependent jobs; never treat an interrupted pair as a win.
